newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police say reported crime drops in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police say reported crime drops in 1996.

text.p: Indonesian police said the number of reported crimes in 1996 dropped nationwide by 6.6 percent despite a string of high-profile felonies through the year, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Speaking at a year-end news conference, national police chief Lieutenant-General Dibyo Widodo said the number of reported cases dropped to 150,806 in 1996 from 166,474 in 1995.
"This means a crime was committed every three minutes and 29 seconds this year, or 14 seconds less often than last year," Widodo was quoted as saying.
He said the province of East Java reported the most crimes with 22,417 cases, followed by West Java with 20,401 cases and the capital Jakarta with 18,830 cases.

The highest profile cases occurred in Jakarta with the escape of jailed bank swindler Eddy Tansil in May, paedophile serial killings in June, the July 27 riot, central bank fraud in August and theft of paintings from the National Museum in September.
"Student brawls, bank customers and taxi driver robberies also marked the city crime this year," Widodo said.
On a per capita basis, North Sulawesi province had the worst crime rate with 251 cases per 100,000 people, followed by the holiday island of Bali with 232 cases and East Kalimantan with 222 cases.
Widodo said in 1996 police had arrested 39 people in 27 Ecstasy cases and seized 337,090 pills, 18 capsules and 2.3 kg of powder.

In other operations, Widodo said 657 foreigners had been arrested for violating immigration laws. Traffic accidents had fallen 6.8 percent to 14,912 from 16,003 cases last year, but the number of injured or killed rose to 10,313 from 9,677 people last year.
